turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Um, well, I guess my manager is the one who really pushed for this. I work as a waitress at this diner, and usually, I'm really good at my job. I went to college for a couple of years, so I'm smart, and I've been serving for a while now, and you know how it gets during a lunch rush—it's just go, go, go. You have to keep a million things in your head at once, the drinks, the modifications, who needs ranch. But lately... well, what really scared everyone at work, and honestly it kind of freaked me out too, is that I just... I started freezing up in the middle of service. 

Like, right in the middle of the floor. Or I'd start doing things completely out of order, which makes no sense because I know the routine backward and forward. The other day, my manager found me just standing over by the soda station. I was just standing there holding the key to the cash drawer, and instead of actually going to the register and closing out my checks like I was supposed to, I was just staring at the syrup boxes and repeating my table numbers out loud. Over and over. "Table four, table seven, table twelve." Just like that. 

And my coworker had to come shake my shoulder because I guess I'd been doing it for a few minutes and the customers were waiting and the checks were just piling up. It's just... it's not like me to mess up the flow like that, but my body just stops, or my brain gets stuck on the numbers, and I can't get to the next step of what I'm supposed to be doing. They told me I needed to get checked out before I could come back on shift because it really freaked out the kitchen staff, too.

I was just stuck there, fully awake, fully aware that I was stuck, but completely unable to break out of the loop until Sarah—she's the coworker who came over—until she actually grabbed my shoulder and physically jolted me out of it.
